A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B support comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original adversarial-training experiments on five LLMs, including GCG/BEAST robustness evaluations, correlation statistics, and utility measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original training and evaluation results and adds robustness results for AmpleGCG and Zhu’s AutoDAN, including appendix figures.

M1.justification: The GCG-based LoRA training procedure, combined safety/utility objective, single-layer linear self-attention model, and surrogate adversarial-training formulation are retained. Expanded explanations and additional evaluation attacks do not introduce a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use HarmBench and Alpaca for training, HarmBench/AdvBench for robustness evaluation, and AlpacaEval for utility evaluation. The added attackers operate within the retained suffix-jailbreaking task and data coverage.

E2.justification: V2 expands the evaluated attack set from GCG and BEAST to include AmpleGCG and Zhu’s AutoDAN across all five LLMs. AmpleGCG’s earlier citation did not constitute evaluation, and Zhu’s AutoDAN is distinct from the Liu et al. AutoDAN already cited in v1.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce an AmpleGCG checkpoint and Zhu’s AutoDAN settings, including T=3, B=256, and temperature 2. Existing splits, suffix-length grids, training budget, and judging procedures are retained. V2 says Adam in Section 5.1 but AdamW in Appendix B.2, so an actual optimizer switch is unresolved.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing cross-attack transfer and suffix-length sensitivity analyses to AmpleGCG and Zhu’s AutoDAN. The earlier GCG/BEAST analyses and utility analysis are retained; relocating their curves into Appendix Figure 4 is not itself additional analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pearson correlations and p-values over 48 length configurations per model–attack pair and use the 0.05 significance threshold. New attack columns follow this existing practice; bold and underlined significance markings are presentation changes. No new seed or repeated-training-run reporting appears.

E6.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 4 and Table 1 add extensive AmpleGCG and Zhu’s AutoDAN results, often showing near-zero post-training ASR. The retained Llama-2/BEAST correlation changes from 0.68 to 0.67, with p-value changing from 1.32 × 10^-7 to 1.68 × 10^-7. GCG correlations and the utility plot are unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma A.5 drops the explicit ordering condition on both singular-value lists while retaining the trace inequality, making its stated premises less explicit. The main assumptions, Theorems 1–2, Corollary 1, and their derivations are otherwise retained; the expanded ICL–LLM bridge is primarily conceptual explanation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that training with suffix length Θ(√M) can defend against length-Θ(M) attacks, supported by an ICL robustness bound and LLM experiments. The abstract’s added resource-cost motivation was already present in v1’s introduction.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds one-hot and padding-token analogies while removing v1’s explicit discussion of the utility-loss mismatch between ICL and LLM training. Section 5.2 newly attributes weak correlations for the added attacks to their nearly zero ASRs after training.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds the specific AmpleGCG checkpoint and access link, plus Zhu’s AutoDAN implementation information and hyperparameters. Existing LoRA settings, training budget, batch composition, evaluation judges, and project-code link are retained, with several details relocated.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Jiongxiao Wang et al. (2023), Zeming Wei et al. (2023), and Sicheng Zhu et al. (2024). The positioning against unrestricted ICL attacks remains intact. AmpleGCG was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: V2 expands the ICL–LLM bridge into Section 4.2, moves training details into Appendix B.2, adds Appendix B.4, and makes localized wording and terminology edits. It also updates authorship and citation style, while retaining most prose and the overall narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different page template, expands Figure 1 and Table 1 to four attacks, and adds significance formatting. The former combined robustness curves become separate attack panels: Vicuna appears in Figure 2 and the other models in Appendix Figure 4. The utility plot is retained but resized.

improvement.justification: Broader attack testing, documented configurations, and separate attack panels provide a modest net improvement. The main theory is unchanged, and near-zero ASRs limit how much the new tests support the length-correlation claim. The Adam/AdamW inconsistency and omitted ordering condition in Lemma A.5 are small losses in precision.
